messages:
Jun Chen: Heads up — product asked to standardize how we surface "Service Identity" vs "Service Key" in the console. Customers keep confusing ownership and quotas.

Maria K: +1. telemetry shows a lot of 429s attributed to 'unknown' identity. We need a clear identity hierarchy (org -> project -> service_account) so quota routing and billing map correctly.

Oliver: can you paste the problematic telemetry snippet so I can see the payload shape?

Maria K: sure, here are a few anonymized examples we see a lot of:
```
{
  "org": null,
  "project": "proj-123",
  "identity_type": "service_key",
  "key_id": null,
  "quota_scope": "org"
}
```

Priya: Oof. null orgs are from legacy tokens lacking project binding. That breaks quota routing when aggregator expects org-level keys. Proposed: require at least one of {org, project, service_account} in token claims, and map legacy unbound tokens to an explicit telemetry tag `legacy_unbound`.

Kate N: UX question — when we show identity in the Console, should it surface "identity owner" (email) or "key owner"? Customers keep asking "who do I ping" when quota spikes. My vote: show contact email + a small badge that says "service identity" vs "one-off key".

Sylvia: From infra side, routing policies rely on token.claims.{org,project,service_account}. If we change required claims we need a migration window. Suggest we add an acceptance header `x-rw-auth-version` and keep a fallback path for 6 months for tokens without the new claim. Avoid hard-fail during rollout.

Infra Bot: deploy queued — canary to eng-platform tomorrow 09:00 PT. :rocket:

Jun Chen: Agree on migration header. Also flagging a current bug in quota calc: our aggregator uses `quota_key = coalesce(project, org, key_id)` which lets legacy keys bleed across projects when project is missing. That causes billing confusion.

Maria K: Suggest we change to `quota_key = if(service_account) concat(org,":",service_account) else if(project) project else key_id`. Simpler mapping and avoids cross-project bleed.

Priya: Another console ask — surface telemetry per-route token-affinity chart + a small table of top ambiguous tokens (counts, first-seen, last-seen) so support can triage quickly.

Oliver: I can prototype an internal endpoint to return ambiguous token aggregates. Proposal: `GET /v1/internal/telemetry/ambiguous-ids?since=24h` returns `{counts_by_type, sample_payloads}`. Keep it internal-only.

Kate N: For rollout UX — we need a console toggle "Enforce project binding" with a warning modal. Default OFF for the first 2 months, then nudge customers. Also add a per-tenant migration report.

Jun Chen: OK next steps: Oliver - prototype endpoint; Maria - add `legacy_unbound` telemetry tag during processing; Priya - wire Console mockups for the toggle and ambiguous-tokens table; Sylvia - implement `x-rw-auth-version` detection and fallback logic; Kate - design the warning modal copy.

Sylvia: I'll also add an ingestion metric `unbound_token_count` to the routing dashboard so SRE can alert on migration progress.

Ops Bot: noted — created ticket RW-PLAT-1452 and assigned to @Oliver, @Maria K, @Priya, @Sylvia, @Kate N.

Maria K: one more ask — telemetry should include the original `token_type` and `issued_at` so we can identify old issuances. small extra cost, big help.

Jun Chen: cool. let's sync tomorrow for 15m after canary. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
